galveosaurus:eswiki:5.title: Galvesaurus herreroi (Controversia del nombre, Galveosaurus o Galvesaurus)

facts.statement: The only known species, G. herreroi, was found in Galve, Spain, which is the origin of its generic name.
facts.quote: Fossils of the only known species, G. herreroi, were found in Galve, Spain, hence its generic name.

facts.statement: Local amateur fossil hunter José María Herrero discovered the fossilized remains of a sauropod at the Cuesta Lonsal site near Galve, Spain, during the 1980s.
facts.quote: During the 1980s, a fossil site known as Cuesta Lonsal, in the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian Villar del Arzobispo Formation near Galve (Teruel), Spain, was excavated by local amateur fossil hunter José María Herrero after he found the fossilized remains of a sauropod dinosaur.

facts.statement: The fossil bones were transferred to the Spanish Paleontological Museum of Galve for display after preparation and study.
facts.quote: As the bones were prepared and studied, the team transferred them to the small Spanish Paleontological Museum of Galve for display.

facts.statement: The Aragosaurus team published a description naming the sauropod Galvesaurus herreroi in the journal Naturaleza Aragonesa.
facts.quote: Barco et al. published their own description of the sauropod, which they named Galvesaurus herreroi (note the lack of the letter "o"), in the journal Naturaleza Aragonesa.

facts.statement: The Aragosaurus team disputed the validity of the name Galveosaurus, arguing that their publication date of July 1, 2005, was valid within the journal's July–December 2005 range.
facts.quote: The Aragosaurus team disputed this, saying that the date given at the end of their paper, July 1, 2005, being within the given July–December range of the journal, was not contradictory and therefore was not sufficient to invoke the ICZN rules.

facts.statement: The Aragosaurus team alleged that Sánchez Hernández knew other scientists were working on the specimen and cited their previous research, suggesting unethical publication practices.
facts.quote: The Aragosaurus team have alleged that Sánchez Hernández must have known other scientists were currently working on the Galve sauropod specimen at the time she published her paper, and note that she even cited one of their previous research papers on the fossil material.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Sánchez Hernández had first-hand access to the specimen, with the Aragosaurus team claiming her photos showed the public display cabinet frame.
facts.quote: Canudo also stated that the wood frame of the display cabinet is visible in one of the photos in Sánchez Hernández's paper, demonstrating that she did not have first-hand access to the specimen and instead relied on the public museum display.

facts.statement: A 2024 phylogenetic analysis recovered Galvesaurus as a sister taxon of Titanosauriformes outside Brachiosauridae.
facts.quote: A 2024 phylogenetic analysis recovered it as a sister taxon of Titanosauriformes outside Brachiosauridae.

facts.statement: Galvesaurus herreroi is the only known species of the extinct genus Galvesaurus, a macronarian sauropod dinosaur that lived approximately 147 million years ago during the Tithonian stage of the Late Jurassic in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: Galvesaurus herreroi es la única especie conocida del género extinto Galvesaurus ("lagarto de Galve") es un dinosaurio saurópodo macronario, que vivió a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 147 millones de años, en el Titoniense, en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: Galveosaurus is a sauropod similar to Cetiosaurus and Barapasaurus, but more advanced.
facts.quote: Galveosaurus es un saurópodo parecido a Cetiosaurus y a Barapasaurus, pero más avanzado.

facts.statement: Galveosaurus was of medium size for a sauropod, measuring 16 meters in length, 4 meters in height, and weighing an estimated 9 tonnes.
facts.quote: Era de tamaño medio, para un saurópodo, con 16 metros de largo, 4 de alto y un peso calculado de 9 toneladas.

facts.statement: Galveosaurus appears to retain many basal characteristics while showing a separate evolutionary line from other sauropod groups.
facts.quote: Al parecer conservan muchas características basales pero mostrando una evolución separada de otras líneas de saurópodos.

facts.statement: The fossil site known as Cuesta Lonsal near Galve, Teruel, Spain, was excavated in the 1980s by amateur fossil hunter José María Herrero.
facts.quote: Durante la década de 1980, un sitio de fósiles conocido como la Cuesta Lonsal, cerca de Galve, Teruel, España, fue excavado por el cazador local de fósiles aficionados José María Herrero

facts.statement: Between 1993 and 2002, researchers recovered more than 50 associated bones belonging to a new sauropod species.
facts.quote: Entre 1993 y 2002, obtuvieron más de 50 huesos asociados con una nueva especie de saurópodo.

facts.statement: The dinosaur was found in the Villar del Arzobispo Formation in Galve, Teruel, Spain, which is the origin of the genus name.
facts.quote: Fue encontrado en la formación Villar del Arzobispo, en Galve, de donde proviene el nombre del género, provincia de Teruel, España.

facts.statement: The species name herreroi honors José María Herrero, who made the discovery.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento lo realizó José María Herrero, por el cual lleva el nombre la especie.

facts.statement: The fossil remains include two humeri, a sternum plate, a scapula, an ischium, a cervical vertebra, a dorsal-caudal vertebra, five caudal vertebrae, a chevron, and rib fragments.
facts.quote: Los restos encontrados incluyen dos húmeros, la placa esternal, una escápula, un isquion, una vértebra cervical, una dorsal-caudal y 5 caudales, un cheurón y fragmentos de costillas

facts.statement: As the bones were prepared and studied, the team transferred them to the small Paleontological Museum of Galve for exhibition.
facts.quote: A medida que los huesos estaban preparados y estudiados, el equipo los transfirió al pequeño Museo Paleontológico de Galve para su exhibición.

facts.statement: The name Galveosaurus herreroi was first published in an article by Bárbara Sánchez-Hernández on August 11, 2005.
facts.quote: El nombre Galveosaurus herreroi, fue publicado por primera vez en un artículo de Bárbara Sánchez-Hernández el 11 de agosto de 2005

facts.statement: The team of Barco et al. published their own description of the sauropod, naming it Galvesaurus herreroi (note the missing 'o'), in the journal Naturaleza Aragonesa.
facts.quote: Barco et al. Publicaron su propia descripción del saurópodo, que llamaron Galvesaurus herreroi, nótese la falta de la letra o, en la revista Naturaleza Aragonesa.

facts.statement: Sánchez-Hernández argued that the publication date for Barco et al. is technically December 31, 2005, citing ICZN articles 21.6 and 23, making her name valid.
facts.quote: Sánchez-Hernández señaló el artículo 21.6 y 23 de ICZN y afirmó que la fecha de publicación de Barco et al. de 2005 se considera técnicamente como el 31 de diciembre de 2005, la última fecha del rango dado.

facts.statement: The "Aragosaurus" team disputed this, stating that the date given at the end of their article, July 1, 2005, was not contradictory within the journal's July to December range.
facts.quote: El equipo de "Aragosaurus" cuestionó esto, diciendo que la fecha dada al final de su artículo, el 1 de julio de 2005, estando dentro del rango dado de julio a diciembre de la revista, no era contradictoria

facts.statement: Canudo claimed that Sánchez-Hernández did not have professional access to the fossils but simply took photos of the bones on display at the museum for her work.
facts.quote: Canudo afirmó que Sánchez-Hernández no tenía acceso profesional al fósiles, pero simplemente fue al museo y tomó fotos de los huesos en exhibición para usar en su trabajo.

facts.statement: While Royo-Torres et al. (2006) placed Galvesaurus within Turiasauria, Barco and Canudo (2012) demonstrated it lacks Turiasauria synapomorphies and is actually a macronarian.
facts.quote: Mientras que Royo-Torres et al. en 2006 colocaron a Galvesaurus dentro de Turiasauria con Losillasaurus y Turiasaurus, Barco y Canudo en 2012 demostraron que Galvesaurus carece de sinapomorfia de Turiasauria, y que en realidad era un macronario.

facts.statement: The parent group of Galveosaurus is Macronaria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Macronaria

facts.statement: Galveosaurus belongs to the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: In the Villar del Arzobispo Formation, bones and tracks of other sauropods, theropods, and ornithopods have been found alongside remains of this species.
facts.quote: En la Formación Villar del Arzobispo, además de los restos de esta especie, han sido hallados huesos e icnitas de otros saurópodos, terópodos y ornitópodos.

facts.statement: The sauropod Losillasaurus was discovered only 80 km from Galve and is of an age close to that of Galveosaurus.
facts.quote: Además el Losillasaurus fue descubierto a tan sólo 80 km de Galve y su edad es próxima a la de Galveosaurus.
